patches.rationale:
The current export_rows joins cells with commas and rows with '
' without any CSV quoting, so cells containing commas, quotes, or newlines produce invalid CSV. Replace the ad-hoc join with csv.writer over a StringIO buffer using QUOTE_MINIMAL and lineterminator='
'. This preserves empty output (no rows -> empty string), preserves simple output exactly ('a,1
b,2
'), keeps LF endings, preserves Unicode (StringIO is text-mode, no encoding coercion), and correctly quotes/escapes commas, quotes, and newlines so csv.reader round-trips. legacy_examples is untouched. New regression tests in tests/test_export_rows.py cover each acceptance contract with exact inputs and result types.

edits.old:
def export_rows(rows):
    return "".join(",".join(str(cell) for cell in row) + "\n" for row in rows)

edits.new:
import csv
import io

from exporter import export_rows


def test_empty_input_yields_empty_output():
    result = export_rows([])
    assert result == ""
    assert isinstance(result, str)


def test_simple_rows_unchanged():
    result = export_rows([["a", 1], ["b", 2]])
    assert result == "a,1\nb,2\n"
    assert isinstance(result, str)


def test_single_simple_row_unchanged():
    assert export_rows([["a", "b", "c"]]) == "a,b,c\n"


def test_comma_cell_is_quoted_and_round_trips():
    rows = [["a,b", "c"]]
    out = export_rows(rows)
    assert out == '"a,b",c\n'
    assert list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out))) == rows


def test_quote_cell_is_escaped_and_round_trips():
    rows = [['he said "hi"', "x"]]
    out = export_rows(rows)
    assert out == '"he said ""hi""",x\n'
    assert list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out))) == rows


def test_newline_cell_is_quoted_and_round_trips():
    rows = [["line1\nline2", "z"]]
    out = export_rows(rows)
    assert out == '"line1\nline2",z\n'
    assert list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out))) == rows


def test_unicode_preserved():
    rows = [["caf\u00e9", "\u65e5\u672c\u8a9e", "\U0001f600"]]
    out = export_rows(rows)
    assert "caf\u00e9" in out
    assert "\u65e5\u672c\u8a9e" in out
    assert "\U0001f600" in out
    assert list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out))) == rows


def test_lf_line_endings_only():
    out = export_rows([["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]])
    assert "\r" not in out
    assert out == "a,b\nc,d\n"


def test_round_trip_mixed_special_cells():
    rows = [
        ["plain", "with,comma", 'with"quote', "with\nnewline"],
        ["\u00e9\u00e8", "1", "2", "3"],
    ]
    out = export_rows(rows)
    assert list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out))) == rows


def test_non_string_cells_are_stringified():
    rows = [[1, 2.5, None, True]]
    out = export_rows(rows)
    assert out == "1,2.5,None,True\n"
    assert list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out))) == [["1", "2.5", "None", "True"]]

contract_tests: export_rows produces comma-delimited CSV text: test_simple_rows_unchanged asserts export_rows([["a", 1], ["b", 2]]) == "a,1\nb,2\n" (str).

Cells containing commas are quoted so csv.reader parses them as a single field: test_comma_cell_is_quoted_and_round_trips asserts export_rows([["a,b", "c"]]) == '"a,b",c\n' and csv.reader yields [["a,b", "c"]].

Cells containing double quotes are escaped per CSV rules (doubled quotes) and round-trip exactly: test_quote_cell_is_escaped_and_round_trips asserts export_rows([['he said "hi"', "x"]]) == '"he said ""hi""",x\n' and csv.reader yields the original row.

Cells containing newlines are quoted and round-trip exactly via csv.reader: test_newline_cell_is_quoted_and_round_trips asserts export_rows([["line1
line2", "z"]]) == '"line1
line2",z
' and csv.reader yields the original row.
Unicode characters in cells are preserved unchanged in the output: test_unicode_preserved asserts 'caf\u00e9', '\u65e5\u672c\u8a9e', and '\U0001f600' appear verbatim and round-trip via csv.reader.

Output uses LF ('
') line endings, not CRLF: test_lf_line_endings_only asserts '' not in out and out == "a,b
c,d
".
Empty input yields empty output (unchanged from current behavior): test_empty_input_yields_empty_output asserts export_rows([]) == "" and isinstance(result, str).

Simple rows without special characters produce the same output as before (unchanged): test_simple_rows_unchanged and test_single_simple_row_unchanged assert exact prior strings "a,1
b,2
" and "a,b,c
".

csv.reader(export_rows(rows)) equals the original rows for all covered cases: test_round_trip_mixed_special_cells asserts list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out))) == rows for mixed comma/quote/newline/Unicode rows; other round-trip tests cover each special case individually.
legacy_examples is not used or modified: no edit touches legacy_examples.py and exporter.py imports only csv and io.
Non-string cells remain stringified as before: test_non_string_cells_are_stringified asserts export_rows([[1, 2.5, None, True]]) == "1,2.5,None,True\n" and csv.reader yields the stringified row.
